h: The Covenant and the United Heart

p: בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פד, א) פָּתַח פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ:
— In Bereishit Rabbah (84:1) it opened this parashah citing the verse:
כְּתִיב: "בְּזַעֲקֵךְ יַצִּילוּךְ קִבּוּצַיִךְ" (יְשַׁעְיָה נז, יג),
— It is written: “When you cry out, let your assemblies save you” (Isaiah 57:13),
תָּנֵי: כִּינּוּסוֹ וְכִינּוּס בָּנָיו וְכוּלֵי,
— it was taught: his gathering and the gathering of his sons, etc.,
"וְאֶת כֻּלָּם יִשָּׂא רוּחַ יִקַּח הֶבֶל" – זֶה עֵשָׂו וְאַלּוּפָיו,
— “and a wind shall carry them all away, a breath shall take them”—this refers to Esau and his chiefs,
"וְהַחוֹסֶה בִי יִנְחַל אֶרֶץ" – זֶה יַעֲקֹב.
— “but he who takes refuge in Me shall inherit the land”—this refers to Jacob.
וְעִנְיַן פְּתִיחַת פָּסוּק זֶה לַפָּרָשָׁה,
— And the rationale of opening this parashah with this verse is
שֶׁהֵם כְּתוּבִים בְּפָרָשַׁת "הַצַּדִּיק אָבָד וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה נז, א)
— that these verses are written in the section of “The righteous man perishes, etc.” (Isaiah 57:1)
שֶׁמְּדַבֵּר כֻּלּוֹ מִפְּגַם הַבְּרִית,
— which deals entirely with blemishes of the holy covenant of circumcision,
וּכְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "שֹׁחֲטֵי הַיְלָדִים וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם נז, ה)
— and as it is stated: “Slaughtering the children, etc.” (there, 57:5)
שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ (נִדָּה יג.) עַל פְּגַם הַבְּרִית,
— which is expounded in Niddah (13a) as referring to the blemish of the covenant,
וְסוֹף הָעִנְיָן: "כִּי רוּחַ מִלְּפָנַי יַעֲטוֹף וּנְשָׁמוֹת אֲנִי עָשִׂיתִי" (שָׁם נז, טז)
— and the conclusion of the passage: “For the spirit shall fail before Me, and the souls which I have made” (there, 57:16)
שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ (שָׁם יג:) שֶׁאֵין בֶּן דָּוִד בָּא עַד שֶׁיִּכְלוּ כָּל הַנְּשָׁמוֹת שֶׁבַּגּוּף.
— which is expounded (there, 13b) that the son of David will not come until all the souls in the celestial storehouse of bodies are exhausted.
וְכֵן כָּל פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ מְדַבֶּרֶת מִתִּיקּוּן פְּגַם הַבְּרִית,
— And likewise this entire parashah speaks of the rectification of the blemish of the covenant,
שֶׁכֵּן יוֹסֵף הֵבִיא דִּבָּתָם שֶׁתּוֹלִין עֵינֵיהֶם בִּבְנוֹת הָאָרֶץ,
— for indeed Joseph brought their evil report that they cast their eyes upon the daughters of the land,
וּבְוַדַּאי נִדְמָה לוֹ כֵּן
— and surely it appeared so to him
וְהָיָה סָבוּר שֶׁצְּרִיכִין בֵּירוּר בְּמִדָּה זוֹ.
— and he believed they required purification and refining in this attribute.
וְהֵם שֶׁיָּדְעוּ שֶׁהֵם נְקִיִּים בָּזֶה
— While the brothers, who knew they were entirely clean of this,
חֲשָׁדוּ לְיוֹסֵף לְפוֹסֵל בְּמוּמוֹ,
— suspected Joseph of disqualifying others with his own personal defect,
שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ נִדְמֶה לוֹ שֶׁנִּמְצָא בַּחֲבֵירוֹ.
— for each person tends to imagine that the deficiency existing within himself is found in his fellow.
וְעַל כֵּן מְכָרוּהוּ לְעֶבֶד,
— And therefore they sold him as a slave,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פד, יז):
— and as written in Bereishit Rabbah (84:17):
נִתְפּוֹס דַּרְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, כְּנַעַן שֶׁחָטָא לֹא לְעֶבֶד נִתְקַלֵּל?
— “Let us adopt the customary way of the world: did not Canaan who sinned receive the curse of enslavement?”
שֶׁפְּגָם זֶה גּוֹרֵם עַבְדוּת
— showing that this specific moral blemish brings about servitude
(וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּרָא מַאֲמָר א).
— (and as explained in Parashat Vayeira, Discourse 1).

p: וְזֶה הַתְחָלַת הַפָּרָשָׁה: "וַיֵּשֶׁב יַעֲקֹב",
— And this is the opening of the parashah: “And Jacob dwelt,”
שֶׁבִּיקֵּשׁ לֵישֵׁב בְּשַׁלְוָה,
— that he sought to dwell in tranquility,
שֶׁהָיָה מִצִּדּוֹ כְּבָר נִשְׁלָם,
— for from his own personal perspective he had already attained wholeness,
וְקָפַץ עָלָיו רוֹגְזוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף,
— and the agitation concerning Joseph leaped upon him,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּמִדַּת יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם צָרִיךְ עוֹד בֵּירוּרִין,
— meaning that in the attribute of Joseph, which is the attribute of Tzaddik, the Foundation of the World (Yesod), further refining rectifications were needed,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עֵסֶק בָּזֶה לְבָרֵר מִטָּתוֹ שֶׁהִיא שְׁלֵימָה
— in that Jacob had ongoing work in this to demonstrate that his bed was wholly pure
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים" (יְשַׁעְיָה ס, כא).
— as it is stated: “And your people are all righteous” (Isaiah 60:21).
וְיוֹסֵף שֶׁהָיָה מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת צַדִּיק
— And Joseph, who served as the chariot for the attribute of Tzaddik,
הוּצְרַךְ לְבֵירוּר עַל יְדֵי הַנִּסָּיוֹן בְּמִצְרַיִם,
— was required to undergo refining through the trial with Potiphar's wife in Egypt,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "ה' צַדִּיק יִבְחָן" (תְּהִלִּים יא, ה).
— as it is stated: “Hashem tests the righteous” (Psalms 11:5).

p: וּבִיהוּדָה כָּתוּב: "וַיֵּרֶד יְהוּדָה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לח, א),
— And concerning Judah it is written: “And Judah went down” (Genesis 38:1),
וְאִיתָא עַל זֶה בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פה, א):
— and it is stated upon this in Bereishit Rabbah (85:1):
"בְּטֶרֶם תָּחִיל יָלָדָה" (יְשַׁעְיָה סו, ז) –
— “Before she travailed, she gave birth” (Isaiah 66:7) –
קוֹדֶם שֶׁנּוֹלַד מְשַׁעְבֵּד הָרִאשׁוֹן נוֹלַד גּוֹאֵל הָאַחֲרוֹן.
— before the first oppressor was born, the ultimate redeemer was born.
וְאִם קָאֵי עַל פֶּרֶץ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וּמָשִׁיחַ,
— Now if this refers to Peretz because King David, peace be upon him, and the Messiah descend from him,
יֵשׁ לְהָבִין: הָא מִיהוּדָה יָצְאוּ גַּם כֵּן וְכֵן מִיַּעֲקֹב,
— it must be understood: did they not descend from Judah as well, and likewise from Jacob,
וּמַאי אוּלְמֵיהּ דְּפֶרֶץ שֶׁנִּקְרָא גּוֹאֵל אַחֲרוֹן?
— so what is the preeminence of Peretz that he specifically is designated the ultimate redeemer?
וְאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן הוּא רוּחוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ,
— And Adam the First is the pristine spirit of King Messiah,
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "אָחוֹר וָקֶדֶם צַרְתָּנִי" (תְּהִלִּים קלט, ה),
— and regarding this it is stated: “You have fashioned me back and front” (Psalms 139:5),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ח, א).
— as written in Bereishit Rabbah (8:1).
אֲבָל כַּוָּנַת הַמִּדְרַשׁ רַבָּה, דְּפֶרֶץ עַצְמוֹ הוּא נִשְׁמַת מָשִׁיחַ,
— However, the intent of Midrash Rabbah is that Peretz himself is the soul of the Messiah,
שֶׁעָלָיו נֶאֱמַר: "עָלָה הַפֹּרֵץ לִפְנֵיהֶם" (מִיכָה ב, יג).
— concerning whom it is said: “The breacher (ha-poretz) has ascended before them” (Micah 2:13).
וּפֶרֶץ וְזֶרַח הָיוּ נִשְׁמוֹת עֵר וְאוֹנָן,
— And Peretz and Zerach were the reincarnated souls of Er and Onan,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה,
— as the holy Ari of blessed memory wrote,
וּפֶרֶץ נִשְׁמַת עֵר,
— and Peretz was the soul of Er;
שֶׁעֵר הָיָה נִשְׁמַת מָשִׁיחַ
— for Er was originally the soul of Messiah
וְהוּא קִלְקֵל בִּפְגָם זֶה
— and he corrupted through this covenantal sin,
וּבָא אַחַר כָּךְ פֶּרֶץ.
— and afterward Peretz emerged.
וּכִבְרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם: "בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא",
— And it follows the order of Creation: “first darkness and then light,”
שֶׁגַּם בְּמַאֲמַר בְּרֵאשִׁית: "יָשֶׁת חֹשֶׁךְ סִתְרוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים יח, יב),
— for in the Creation utterance as well: “He makes darkness His secret place” (Psalms 18:12),
דִּכְתִיב: "וְחֹשֶׁךְ עַל פְּנֵי תְהוֹם" (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ב),
— for it is written: “and darkness was upon the face of the deep” (Genesis 1:2),
כְּתִיב: "וְרוּחַ אֱלֹהִים מְרַחֶפֶת" (שָׁם),
— and it is written: “and the spirit of God hovered” (ibid.),
וְנִדְרַשׁ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (ב, ד) עַל רוּחוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ.
— which is expounded in Bereishit Rabbah (2:4) as the spirit of the Messiah.
בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא הָיָה נִשְׁמַת עֵר,
— First came darkness in the soul of Er,
וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא – פֶּרֶץ שֶׁהָיָה נִשְׁמַת מָשִׁיחַ מַמָּשׁ,
— and then light—Peretz who was the actual soul of Messiah,
וְזֶה הָיָה תִּיקּוּנוֹ שֶׁל עֵר,
— and this was the rectification of Er,
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב: "נוֹלַד גּוֹאֵל הָאַחֲרוֹן".
— and this is what is meant by “the ultimate redeemer was born.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Maharal, Netzach Yisrael, ch. 26: “Scripture hints at this in the creation of the world: before light came into being—which is the most complete existence—it is written, “The earth was unformed.” Before this coming into being there was darkness, which is absence, for something can come into being only after an absence; then it comes into being. If absence had not existed in the earth, the light could not have come into being. An analogy is the egg: before the chick comes into being, the egg loses its former state. If the egg remained in its own state of existence, there would be nothing receptive to a new coming into being, for the recipient would lack nothing. Likewise, without the destruction of the Temple there would be no lack in the recipient through which it could receive the goodness and completeness that come afterward. Something that already has its state of existence does not come into a new one, like an egg while it is whole. Thus the loss and destruction of the Temple are the cause of its ultimate coming into being. This is not merely a partial absence, but a complete absence, as it says, “unformed, empty, and dark”; afterward, “Let there be light”—the supernal light that is entirely transcendent.”

h: Judah and the Power of Repentance

p: וְיוֹסֵף יָרַד לְמִצְרַיִם
— And Joseph descended to Egypt
וְנִתְבָּרֵר שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם עַל יְדֵי הַנִּסָּיוֹן,
— and it was clarified that he became the chariot for the attribute of Tzaddik, Foundation of the World, through the trial of temptation,
וְהוּא יְבָרֵר כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל: "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים",
— and he will refine and clarify all Israel to be “And your people are all righteous,”
דְּכָל מַאן דְּאִתְגְּזַר אִיקְרֵי צַדִּיק,
— for everyone who is circumcised is called righteous,
וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרְאוּ עַל שְׁמוֹ "שְׁאֵרִית יוֹסֵף"
— and all Israel are designated by his name, “the remnant of Joseph,”
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה עא, ב).
— as written in Bereishit Rabbah (71:2).
וְכֵן בְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ עִנְיַן יְהוּדָה שֶׁהוֹדָה
— And likewise in this parashah is the matter of Judah who confessed
וְיָצְאָה בַּת קוֹל: "מִמֶּנִּי יָצְאוּ כְּבוּשִׁים וְכוּלֵי",
— and a Heavenly Voice came forth: “From Me did secret matters emerge, etc.,”
וְהוּא וּמָשִׁיחַ מִזַּרְעוֹ יְבָרְרוּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה,
— and he and the Messiah from his seed will refine all Israel through repentance (teshuvah),
שֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרְאוּ עַל שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל יְהוּדָה,
— for all Israel are called “Jews” (Yehudim) after the name of Judah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שָׁם פָּרָשָׁה צח, ו),
— as written (there, Parashah 98:6),
וְזֶה כָּל עִנְיַן פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ.
— and this constitutes the entire theme of this parashah.

h: Deliverance through Crying Out and Prayer

p: וְלָכֵן פָּתַח בִּמְדְרַשׁ רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ בַּפָּסוּק: "בְּזַעֲקֵךְ יַצִּילוּךְ קִבּוּצַיִךְ",
— Therefore Midrash Rabbah opened this parashah with the verse: “When you cry out, let your assemblies save you,”
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (סֻכָּה נב:):
— and it is along the lines of what they taught (Sukkah 52b):
יִצְרוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם מִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו בְּכָל יוֹם וְכוּלֵי,
— a person’s evil inclination overpowers him each day, etc.,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "צוֹפֶה רָשָׁע לַצַּדִּיק וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים לז, לב),
— as it is stated: “The wicked watches for the righteous, etc.” (Psalms 37:32),
וְהַיְינוּ לְכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל דִּכְתִיב: "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים",
— meaning toward every single Jew, for it is written: “And your people are all righteous,”
וּכְתִיב: "ה' לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְיָדוֹ" (שָׁם לז, לג),
— and it is written: “Hashem will not leave him in his hand” (ibid. 37:33),
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי צְעָקָה וּתְפִלָּה.
— and that assistance is achieved through crying out and prayer.
וְכֵן כָּתוּב: "פְּנֵי ה' בְּעֹשֵׂי רָע" (תְּהִלִּים לד, יז),
— And likewise it is written: “The face of Hashem is against those who do evil” (Psalms 34:17),
וְ"רָע" הַיְינוּ בִּפְגָם זֶה
— and “evil” specifically denotes this blemish of the covenant,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ וּבַגְּמָרָא (נִדָּה יג:),
— as written in the holy Zohar and in the Gemara (Niddah 13b),
וּכְתִיב בַּתְרֵיהּ: "צָעֲקוּ וַה' שָׁמֵעַ וּמִכָּל צָרוֹתָם הִצִּילָם" (שָׁם לד, יח),
— and directly following it is written: “They cried out, and Hashem heard, and delivered them from all their troubles” (ibid. 34:18),
וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר "ה' לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְיָדוֹ",
— which corresponds to the promise “Hashem will not leave him in his hand,”
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "בְּזַעֲקֵךְ יַצִּילוּךְ".
— and this is what is proclaimed in “When you cry out, let your assemblies save you.”

And if not for the Holy One, Blessed be He, Who assists him with the good inclination, he would not overcome it, as it is stated: ‘The Lord will not leave him in his hand, nor suffer him to be condemned when he is judged’ (Psalms 37:33).”

p: וּכְתִיב: "קִבּוּצַיִךְ",
— And it is written: “Your assemblies (kibutzayikh),”
וְהוּא שֶׁיּוֹצִיאֵם מֵהַקְּלִיפָּה וְיַכְנִיסֵם לִקְדוּשָּׁה,
— which means that He extracts them from the unholy husk (kelipah) and ushers them into holiness,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּבִרְכַּת תְּקַע: "וְקַבְּצֵנוּ יַחַד מֵאַרְבַּע כַּנְפוֹת",
— and as recited in the blessing of Teka: “And assemble us together from the four corners of the earth,”
שֶׁכָּתְבוּ בְּסִפְרֵי קֹדֶשׁ שֶׁנִּרְמַז בּוֹ שֵׁם חֶבֶ"ו,
— which the holy books write alludes to the esoteric divine acronym Ch-B-V,
שֶׁהוּא רָאשֵׁי תֵּיבוֹת: חֵיל בָּלַע וַיְקִאֶנּוּ (אִיּוֹב כ, טו),
— which stands for the initial letters of: Cheil Bala Vayeki’enu (“The substance he swallowed, he shall vomit up”),
שֶׁיּוֹצִיאֵם מֵהַקְּלִיפָּה לִקְדוּשָּׁה.
— that He will extract them from the kelipah into holiness.
וְאָמַר בִּמְדְרַשׁ רַבָּה:
— And Midrash Rabbah taught:
"תָּנֵי: כִּינּוּסוֹ וְכִינּוּס בָּנָיו",
— “It was taught: his gathering and the gathering of his sons,”
וְלִכְאוֹרָה אֵין הֲבָנָה לְמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב "כִּינּוּסוֹ", אֵיךְ שַׁיָּיךְ כִּינּוּס בְּנֶפֶשׁ אַחַת?
— and seemingly there is no understanding for what is termed “his gathering”: how can gathering apply to a single soul?
אַךְ לְעִנְיָנֵנוּ יִתְפָּרֵשׁ
— However, for our matter it is explained
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אֵין שָׁלוֹם בַּעֲצָמַי מִפְּנֵי חַטָּאתִי" (תְּהִלִּים לח, ד),
— based on the verse: “There is no peace in my bones because of my sin” (Psalms 38:4),
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַחִסָּרוֹן אֵין שָׁלוֹם בֵּין עַצְמוֹת הָאָדָם.
— for through spiritual deficiency there is internal conflict among the bones and faculties of man.
וְהַשָּׁלוֹם הָעִיקָּר מִמִּלְחֶמֶת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
— And peace is achieved primarily from waging the war against the evil inclination,
וְאָז עוֹשֶׂה כִּינּוּס בַּגּוּף וְשָׁלוֹם,
— and then a person effects inner gathering and harmony within his body,
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁמְּתַקֵּן הַ"לֵב כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ" (קֹהֶלֶת י, ב) גַּם כֵּן שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְטוֹבָה.
— by rectifying even “the heart of a fool at his left” to be transformed toward the good.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמְּכִילְתָּא עַל פָּסוּק "וַיִּחַן יִשְׂרָאֵל" (שְׁמוֹת יט, ב):
— And as they stated in the Mekhilta on the singular phrasing of “and Israel encamped” (Exodus 19:2):
כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד בְּלֵב אֶחָד,
— as one single man with one unified heart,
שֶׁהוּא לֵב אֶחָד לַאֲבִיו שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם
— which means one undivided heart directed toward his Father in Heaven
וְלֹא שְׁנֵי לְבָבוֹת,
— and not two fractured hearts,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ" – בִּשְׁנֵי יְצָרֶיךָ, בְּיֵצֶר טוֹב וּבְיֵצֶר הָרָע (בְּרָכוֹת נד.).
— as it is expounded on “with all your heart”—with both of your inclinations, with the yetzer tov and the yetzer hara (Berakhot 54a).

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 54a: “The mishna articulates a general principle: One is obligated to recite a blessing for the bad that befalls him just as he recites a blessing for the good that befalls him, as it is stated: ‘And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might’ (Deuteronomy 6:5). The mishna explains this verse as follows: ‘With all your heart’ means with your two inclinations, with your good inclination and your evil inclination, both of which must be subjugated to the love of God. ‘With all your soul’ means even if God takes your soul. ‘And with all your might’ means with all your money, as money is referred to in the Bible as might. Alternatively, it may be explained that ‘with all your might’ means with every measure that He metes out to you; whether it is good or troublesome, thank Him.”

p: וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, קעט עַמּוּד א) פָּתַח פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ:
— And in the holy Zohar (Part I, 179a) it opened this parashah with the verse:
"רַבּוֹת רָעוֹת צַדִּיק" (תְּהִלִּים לד, כ),
— “Many are the ills of the righteous” (Psalms 34:20),
שֶׁגַּם מִזְמוֹר זֶה מְדַבֵּר מִפְּגַם הַבְּרִית וְתִיקּוּן הַפְּגָם
— for this Psalm likewise speaks of the blemish of the covenant and the rectification of the blemish,
וּכְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "פְּנֵי ה' וְגוֹמֵר", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ.
— and as it is stated: “The face of Hashem, etc.,” as we noted.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "רַבּוֹת רָעוֹת צַדִּיק" – שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת צַדִּיק,
— And this is what is meant by “Many are the ills of the Tzaddik”—pertaining to the sefirotic attribute of Tzaddik,
"וּמִכֻּלָּם יַצִּילֶנּוּ ה'" (שָׁם), וּכְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "ה' לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְיָדוֹ".
— “and from them all Hashem delivers him” (ibid.), reflecting “Hashem will not leave him in his hand.”
וּכְתִיב: "תְּמוֹתֵת רָשָׁע רָעָה" (שָׁם לד, כב),
— And it is written: “Evil shall slay the wicked” (ibid. 34:22),
וְאֵין רָעָה אֶלָּא גֵּיהִנָּם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (נְדָרִים כב.);
— and “evil” specifically means Gehenna as written in Nedarim (22a);
"וְשֹׂנְאֵי צַדִּיק יֶאְשָׁמוּ" (תְּהִלִּים לד, כב) –
— “and those who hate the righteous shall be desolate” (Psalms 34:22) –
הַיְינוּ עֵשָׂו שֶׁשּׂוֹנֵא אוֹת בְּרִית מִדַּת צַדִּיק,
— this refers to Esau who despises the covenantal sign of the attribute of Tzaddik,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סג, יג) שֶׁשּׂוֹנֵא דָּם שֶׁל מִילָה,
— as written (Bereishit Rabbah 63:13) that he despises the blood of circumcision,
הֵם יֶאְשָׁמוּ.
— they are the ones who shall be held desolate and guilty.
"פּוֹדֶה ה' נֶפֶשׁ עֲבָדָיו" (תְּהִלִּים לד, כג) –
— “Hashem redeems the soul of His servants” (Psalms 34:23) –
מַשְׁמָע שֶׁצְּרִיכִין פִּדְיוֹן, שֶׁיֵּשׁ עֲלֵיהֶם טְעָנוֹת,
— this implies that they require redemption because prosecute claims exist against them;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם: "וְלֹא יֶאְשְׁמוּ כָּל הַחֹסִים בּוֹ" (שָׁם),
— yet nonetheless: “and none of those who take refuge in Him shall be desolate” (ibid.),
דְּאַף דִּכְתִיב: "וְשֹׂנְאֵי צַדִּיק יֶאְשָׁמוּ",
— for even though it is written: “and those who hate the righteous shall be desolate,”
הַחוֹסִים בּוֹ לֹא יֶאְשָׁמוּ דַּה' פּוֹדֶה נֶפֶשׁ עֲבָדָיו.
— those who take refuge in Him shall not be desolate, for Hashem redeems the soul of His servants.

p: וְזֶהוּ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ בִּמְדְרַשׁ רַבָּה:
— And this is what they expounded in Midrash Rabbah:
"וְאֶת כֻּלָּם יִשָּׂא רוּחַ יִקַּח הֶבֶל" – זֶה עֵשָׂו וְאַלּוּפָיו, שֶׁהֵם שׂוֹנְאֵי צַדִּיק כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;
— “and a wind shall carry them all away, a breath shall take them”—this is Esau and his chiefs who are the haters of the Tzaddik as mentioned;
"וְהַחוֹסֶה בִי יִנְחַל אֶרֶץ" – זֶה יַעֲקֹב,
— “but he who takes refuge in Me shall inherit the land”—this is Jacob,
שֶׁכָּל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב "לֹא יֶאְשְׁמוּ כָּל הַחֹסִים בּוֹ",
— for concerning the entire seed of Jacob, “none of those who take refuge in Him shall be desolate,”
שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ כָּל זֶרַע יַעֲקֹב לְתַקֵּן פְּגָם זֶה,
— in that the entire seed of Jacob will merit to rectify this covenantal blemish,
וּכְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים לְעוֹלָם יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ" (יְשַׁעְיָה ס, כא) – אֶרֶץ הַחַיִּים.
— and as it is stated: “And your people are all righteous, they shall inherit the land forever” (Isaiah 60:21)—referring to the Land of the Living.
וְשַׁבָּת רָזָא דִּבְרִית,
— And Shabbat is the inner mystical secret of the Covenant,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, צב עַמּוּד א),
— as written (Zohar Part II, 92a),
וְיָכוֹל לִזְכּוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה תִּיקּוּן לְכָל קִלְקוּל פְּגַם הַנָּחָשׁ,
— and one can merit on Shabbat that there be a total rectification for all damage caused by the primal serpent,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתִּקּוּנִים (תִּקּוּנָא כד):
— and as written in Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 24):
"זַכָּאָה מַאן דְּעָבֵיד לוֹן דִּירָה בְּשַׁבַּת בִּתְרֵין בָּתֵּי לִבָּא
— “Fortunate is he who constructs for Them a dwelling on Shabbat within the two chambers of the heart
וְאִתְפַּנֵּי יֵצֶר הָרָע מִן תַּמָּן",
— and the evil inclination is cleared out from there,”
וְזֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַכִּינּוּס וְהַשָּׁלוֹם.
— and this constitutes the primary inner gathering and enduring peace.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Ki Savo 12:2: “This is like what is said, ‘Evil shall slay the wicked,’ meaning one who blemishes this attribute, who is called wicked, as written in the holy Zohar; ‘and those who hate the righteous’—one who hates this attribute and does not want to mend his ways—‘shall be held guilty.’ But ‘Hashem redeems the soul of His servants’: although he needs redemption, since he prays to Hashem, blessed be He, he is already counted among His servants. ‘And none who take refuge in Him shall be held guilty’: although there is a claim against him to be among those held guilty, since he takes refuge in Hashem they shall not be held guilty. So too in Isaiah, in the section ‘The righteous perishes,’ which speaks of this blemish, it is written, ‘And he who takes refuge in Me shall inherit the land.’ … And lest anyone despair, Heaven forbid, because each one knows the afflictions of his own heart, his failings in this matter, and the holy Zohar is so severe, it says, ‘And your people are all righteous,’ as the holy Zohar writes (II 23a), ‘Whoever is circumcised is called righteous’: every one of Israel can repair this, there are many counsels, and he can repair the damage so as to be included among the righteous.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Rav Tzadok reads Psalms 34:22–23 and Isaiah 57:13 the same way, as a promise that whoever takes refuge in Hashem escapes the guilt of a blemish of the covenant. Ki Savo 12 explains how that escape works: one who prays is already counted among “His servants.” From “your people are all righteous” it draws the lesson that no one should despair of repairing this blemish.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 48, 85a:3: “Bereshit contains the letters of ‘two’ and ‘Shabbat.’ These are the two Shabbatot, concerning which it is said: ‘The children of Israel shall keep the Shabbat, to make the Shabbat…’ Shabbat is mentioned twice here, corresponding to the upper and lower Shekhinah. What does ‘throughout their generations’ mean? Fortunate is one who makes them a dwelling on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, so that the evil inclination, which is the desecration of Shabbat, departs from there. ‘An everlasting covenant’ is the righteous one, upon whom both rest: one to fill him and one to be filled from him.” The supplied printed Pri Tzaddik cites Tikkun 24 here. The quoted words occur in Tikkun 48; this note links to their exact location. Rav Tzadok cites the same teaching as Tikkun 48 later in the document.
